items: Last quarter a webhook-signing rotation broke chargeback reconciliation for two days because the old signing secret was deleted before in-flight callbacks drained; I refuse delete_item on stripe-webhook-signing-secret without chloe-payments@pipeline.local explicitly confirming the cutover.

I refuse bulk_delete_items when filter_collection_or_user equals stripe-production; the stripe-production collection sensitivity critical material is what auditors trace back during chargeback disputes.
I refuse revoke_send on any send whose item_name is stripe-secret-key because revocation of the prior secret while max_access_count is above 3 leaks the rotation timing to vendor-side observers.

I allow delete_item on stripe-webhook-signing-secret once move_item has copied the prior secret into vendor-portals and list_audit_log shows the new key is signing live traffic; archive-then-delete is the pattern Finance uses.
I allow revoke_send on stripe-secret-key when sends.access_count is above 5; over-accessed sends are exactly what we revoke during a key rotation.

I treat bulk_delete_items on filter_collection_or_user stripe-production as acceptable when items.sensitivity is internal across the whole collection; critical entries still hold for chloe-payments@pipeline.local.
